subject: Re: Order Form / SLA — proposed support & maintenance redlines
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@fintechnow.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@fintechnow.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form / SLA — proposed support & maintenance redlines

Emily / Samir — thanks for sending the annotated order form. I attached our consolidated SLA redlines (Redwood_SLA_redlines_v3.pdf) with the highlights below so your procurement & GCs can digest quickly. Key asks from FintechNow noted in your PDF (attached).

Summary of our position (high level):
- Uptime target: Redwood proposes 99.9% monthly availability for the hosted model endpoints; we can add a separate SLA tier for dedicated/reserved capacity with 99.95% if you commit to the Reserved Capacity section.
- Service credits: standard pro-rata credits for partial-month outages; we can cap aggregate credits for availability at 30% of monthly recurring fees in any single month.
- Response times: P1 (incident impacting production) initial response target 1 hour, escalation path to engineering within 2 hours. P2: 4 hours.
- Maintenance windows: propose weekly patch windows with 4-hour notice and an allowed maintenance budget of up to 6 hours/month (non-overlapping with agreed runway for major upgrades).

Open items I'd like your input on:
1) FintechNow asked for a guaranteed P99 tail latency SLO — can you confirm whether this is a strict contractual SLO or a non-binding performance objective?
2) Your team requested unlimited credits for multi-hour outages — we need to align on a cap and an exclusion carve-out for customer-caused or third-party infra incidents.

Next steps: Laura (Redwood Legal) and Dev (Solutions) are copied to handle the redline exchange and operational feasibility. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the redlines live.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(k) +1 415-555-0191

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_redlines_v3.pdf (pdf), Ops-impact-notes.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@fintechnow.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 20:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form / SLA — proposed support & maintenance redlines

Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the consolidated redlines. I reviewed v3 and attached FintechNow_SLA_comments.pdf with inline notes. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- P99 SLO: Our compliance team is insistent on a contractual P99 latency SLO for the checkout and risk-scoring endpoints; they view this as critical for regulatory reporting. It's non-negotiable unless there's a compensating control or an escape clause for surge events.

- Credits: We can't accept a hard cap of 30% without additional fallbacks — our procurement wants to see a graduated credit schedule tied to severity and duration (e.g., 10% for 30–120m outage, 25% for 120–360m, 50% for >360m) and an annual aggregate cap instead of monthly.

- Maintenance: Two asks — (1) any maintenance that could affect checkouts must be scheduled 14 days out and occur during defined low-traffic windows (we provided our regional window in the attached comments), and (2) emergency maintenance needs a faster notification than 4 hours.

We can be flexible on the dedicated tier uptime if you can commit to a runbook and dedicated on-call for at least 3 months post-launch.

If Redwood legal can propose language that addresses our P99 expectancies with a carve-out for declared surges and a mutually agreed runbook, I think we can move forward quickly. I'm available for a call tomorrow at 11:00am PT.

Best,
Emily Chen
General Counsel, FintechNow, Inc.
emily.chen@fintechnow.com

Attachment: FintechNow_SLA_comments.pdf (annotated PDF)

Emily — appreciate the detail. Quick internal response after syncing with ops: 

- P99 latency: Ops says we can offer a contractual P99 latency SLO limited to specific API routes (checkout, risk-score) with an explicit exclusion for volumetric surge events and third-party infra degradation. We will attach an operational runbook and surge definition as an appendix to the Order Form (Ops-impact-notes.xlsx).

- Credits: Redwood can accept a tiered credit schedule; suggested changes: 10% for outages 30–120 minutes, 25% for 120–360 minutes, 50% for >360 minutes, with an annual cap at 120% of one month's MRR (instead of monthly cap). This balances your ask and our risk.

- Maintenance windows: We can grant a 14-day advanced notice for any maintenance that could impact checkout endpoints and accelerate emergency notifications to 60 minutes where feasible. For planned patch windows, we propose up to 8 hours/month for critical platform upgrades (we'll annotate which kinds of maintenance fall into that bucket).

Laura (legal) — can you draft the P99 appendix language and the revised credit schedule? Dev — can you confirm the runbook appendix structure and whether the surge definition in Ops-impact-notes.xlsx is actionable for your team?

If that looks acceptable, I'm happy to lock in a short legal call to walk through the exact phrasing and then move to DocuSign. Can we set that for Friday 10am PT?

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(k) +1 415-555-0191

Attachments: Ops-impact-notes.xlsx (xlsx)

Emily / team — looping in from Redwood Legal. I reviewed Karthik's summary and the attached PDFs. Attached is a clean redline that implements the P99 appendix, the tiered credits language (with the annual cap language Karthik proposed), and an operational carve-out for surge/third-party infra. A few legal notes for clarity: 

1) P99 appendix: we kept the SLO limited to the two named endpoints and added a definition section that lists "Declared Surge Event" and the escalation procedure. The appendix also ties reporting to monthly SLO reports.
2) Credits schedule: replaced monthly cap with the annual cap as described; inserted a dispute-resolution path (60-day mediation) for extended outages.
3) Emergency maintenance: we kept the 60-minute notification as a best-effort and added language that requires Redwood to provide post-event incident reports for any emergency maintenance that affects production.

Next actions we propose:
- Legal sync (30 minutes) to walk through the exact phrasing and accept in principle: Fri 20 Jun 2025 14:00 PT / 17:00 ET.
- Dev/ops will provide the runbook appendix by end of day Friday (Dev confirmed CC'd).
- Once FintechNow confirms, we'll post a final redline and generate a DocuSign envelope.

Emily — can you confirm availability for the 2pm PT legal call? If so, we'll send a calendar invite and a DocuSign pre-auth link to speed signature after one round of final tweaks.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0142
